title: Investigate prefill/decode interleaving and hybrid FlashAttention integration to recover long-context throughput regression
creator: Aisha Mirza
description: Summary: After merging the hybrid FlashAttention v2/v3 integration and the new prefill prober, internal benchmarks show a 12-18% throughput regression for long-context workloads (seq_len >= 16k) in prefill-heavy traffic patterns. This ticket aims to investigate whether the regression is caused by: 1) suboptimal kernel selection when interleaving prefill + decode requests, 2) cache/kv-buffer thrashing introduced by the prober's warmup sequences, or 3) micro-tiling choices that favor v3 kernels at the cost of v2 performance on certain GPUs. Goals: reproduce regression across hardware variants, identify root cause(s), propose and implement mitigations, and prepare a rollback/canary plan.
notes:
Observations so far:
- Regression reproduces on Ampere A100 and Hopper H100 in our perf lab but is absent on some older T4 tests.
- Microbenchmarks indicate FlashAttn v3 has lower latency for medium sequences (<4k) but exhibits worse memory locality for >12k sequences when the prober runs prefill warmups.
- The prober currently injects short prefill-only batches to gather kernel selection stats; these warmups appear to evict long-lived KV cache entries on hosts running multiple tenants.
- Canary on dedicated pool with stricter KV pinning recovers ~7% of the lost throughput, suggesting cache eviction is a contributor.
- Speculative fallback to v2 for long-context paths recovers up to 13% but increases decode latencies for short-turn workloads.

Proposed investigation plan:
1) Reproduce with deterministic load generator: build two scenarios (prefill-heavy and decode-heavy) at seq_len 8k/12k/16k/32k across GPU variants. Collect kernel selection traces, KV cache hit-rate, and allocator churn.
2) Add prober off flag and run A/B to confirm prober's impact.
3) Instrument kernel selector to expose tiling heuristic scores and selection reasons in traces.
4) Evaluate lightweight KV pinning strategy to prevent short warmups from evicting long-prefill caches.
5) Implement 'long-context override' in routing policy: prefer v2 or a v3-large-tile variant for requests with seq_len >= threshold.
6) Run end-to-end canary (10% traffic) with metrics and rollback playbook.

Success criteria:
- Reproduce and attribute >=80% of regression to identified cause(s) or combination of causes.
- Implement mitigation that recovers >=10% throughput without increasing tail latency beyond existing SLOs.
- Canary shows no user-facing correctness regressions and acceptable cost delta.

Deliverables:
- Root cause write-up (Confluence)
- PR(s) with prober toggle + KV pinning + kernel-selection override rules
- Canary dashboard and rollback runbook
- Postmortem if rollback required
